thread:
Maya: Quick recap from the call with Azure earlier — they pushed a spend-based EDP but the capacity language is 'best-effort' for specific GPU SKUs. We need a firm ask on guarantees or compensating credits.

Lena (Azure-Rep): From our side: we can commit to spend tiers and provide regional floors, but per-SKU hard reservations are limited. We can add credits for preemption >5% and a 72-hour burst window.

Tom (eng-sre): 5% preemptions is a non-starter for our latency-sensitive model serving. That would kill some of our SLAs. We need <=1% or a contract-level fallback (automatic routing to reserved pool or alternate region) without extra traffic egress/burst charges.

Arjun (finance): Numbers to consider: our current on-demand GPU spend is ~ $1.8M/yr. Azure's EDP draft was ~$1.2M/yr over 3 years for a tier that *might* give us priority access. If they insist on best-effort, we should demand credits sized to cover failed capacity impact. Also require invoice-level metering.

Lena (Azure-Rep): I hear you. Options we can push internally: (1) regional capacity floor (commit X GPUs reserved in region), (2) guaranteed non-preemptible carveouts for a subset of instances, or (3) credits for unmet commitments. Azure legal prefers credit language over hard failover guarantees, but ops can escalate.

Maya: We should propose concrete contract language. Draft suggestion below — open to edits: 
```
If Provider fails to allocate reserved GPU capacity in Customer's selected region such that Customer's reserved instances are not provisionable for >72 continuous hours during a calendar quarter, Provider will either: 
  (a) provision equivalent reserved capacity in a Provider-adjacent region within 24 hours at no additional charge (customer bandwidth and egress costs waived), or 
  (b) issue a service credit equal to 10x the affected hourly GPU rate for each impacted GPU-hour.
```

SRE-Bot: ALERT: us-west2 preemption spike detected — 6 preemptions in last 2h (models-serving-prod). Log id: `preempt-20240712-usc`.

Tom (eng-sre): See — this is exactly the failure scenario. We need explicit carveouts for preemption-sensitive workloads. Suggested: allow Customer to designate up to N% of committed capacity as non-preemptible (pin to a dedicated pool) with a small premium if needed.

Arjun (finance): Also: metering clarity. We cannot accept opaque billing. Ask for per-GPU-hour metering, raw usage exports (CSV/BigQuery), and a 90-day audit window. If vendor pushes per-instance-hour only, we need SKU-to-GPU mapping in writing.

Lena (Azure-Rep): We can provide raw metering exports (CSV) and a 90-day export window — I'll confirm with billing. Legal has pushed back on unrestricted audits but will accept structured audit rights with 30-day notice.

Maya: Action items: (1) I'll circulate the draft clause above and a short bullet list of asks to the rep: hard regional floors, 1% preemption target or non-preemptible carveout, per-GPU-hour metering + raw exports, and explicit credit formula. (2) @Nina (legal) and @Raj (contracts) to review.

Nina (legal): On it — will review the clause and propose tweaks around liability caps and waterfall remedies. We should avoid open-ended egress indemnities.

Tom (eng-sre): Also ask for a capacity ramp schedule in the EDP (months 1/6/12 targets) and a defined escalation path (ops on-call + named account engineering contact).

Maya: Good call. I'll add ramp schedule and named AE/SE to the email.

Lena (Azure-Rep): I'll escalate the non-preemptible carveout to our infra team. Expect an update by EOD tomorrow.

Maya: Thanks — I'll draft the vendor email now and post the thread. Ping me if you want to add precise numbers for the regional floor or non-preemptible count.

Arjun (finance): I'll run stress numbers overnight and propose two commitment bands (conservative + aggressive).

Maya: Perfect. Closing for now — will share the email draft here by EOD. :thumbsup:
